Method call arguments must declare their parameter names.

What The Standard says

“Level 0” — The Standard requires code to be understandable by entry-level engineers. Named arguments expose the meaning of each value without requiring the reader to navigate to the called method. read it here.
“collector” — The validation collector examples name arguments such as message, rule and parameter to keep dense rule construction readable. The analyser generalizes that canonical style. read it here.

Why it matters

Named arguments reveal the contract of a call at its point of use, particularly where several values share a type. This supports the Standard's preference for self-explanatory code and reduces mistakes caused by positional ordering.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT005: Method call arguments must declare their parameter names.
service.AddStudent(student, true);

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT005
service.AddStudent(newStudent: student, notify: true);
